newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates steady on select trade.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates steady on select trade.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates were steady on Sunday as spinners opted to wait for a relief package the caretaker government is likely to announce for the textile industry, dealers said.

Caretaker Comerce Minister Zubair Khan said on Saturday the government was considering to revise duties on the import of raw cotton and synthetic fibres not produced in Pakistan to help the textile industry cope with a domestic cotton crop shortfall. Pakistan's 1996/97 (July/June) cotton crop is estimated to reach 9.2 to 9.5 million 375-lb bales, down from a target of 10 million bales and the 1995/96 crop of 9.96 million bales.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,150 rupees ($53.45) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
